reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification (display-math fragments judged with the line they belong to).
0001-0003 Setup: fix feasible flows f,g with |g|>|f|, announce construction of h in Gf with |h|=|g|-|f|. Justified restatement of the goal.
0004-0005 Recalls the residual network: each original edge (u,v) contributes forward arc (u,v) with cf=c(u,v)-f(u,v) and backward arc (v,u) with cf=f(u,v). This is the standard construction; residual arcs are indexed per original edge, so antiparallel original edges give parallel residual arcs (the h(u,v) notation is then ambiguous, but each residual arc still receives a single well-defined value). Acceptable.
0006-0007 Defines h edge-by-edge on original edges by comparing g(u,v) with f(u,v). Well-posed: the two cases are exhaustive and mutually exclusive per edge.
0008-0009 Case g>=f: h(u,v):=g(u,v)-f(u,v) on the forward arc. Legitimate assignment, nonnegative.
0010-0012 Case g<f: h(v,u):=f(u,v)-g(u,v) on the backward arc of that same edge. Legitimate, nonnegative.
0013 Residual arcs not touched by the two cases get h=0. Completes the definition of h on all of E(Gf).
0014-0016 Informal gloss of h as the excess of g over f, and statement of what remains to prove (capacity, conservation, value). No claim needing proof.
0017-0018 Nonnegativity of h on forward arcs: immediate from the case condition g(u,v)>=f(u,v). Correct.
0019-0020 h(u,v)=g(u,v)-f(u,v)<=c(u,v)-f(u,v)=cf(u,v) using g(u,v)<=c(u,v) (feasibility of g). Correct.
0021-0023 Backward arcs: 0<=f(u,v)-g(u,v)<=f(u,v)=cf(v,u) using g(u,v)>=0. Correct.
0023-0025 Remaining arcs carry 0<=cf, hence 0<=h(e)<=cf(e) everywhere; capacity constraints hold. Correct conclusion from the three cases, which exhaust E(Gf).
0026-0028 Announces conservation at every x not in {s,t} and fixes such an x. Fine.
0029-0036 Conservation of f at x: sum of f on edges out of x equals sum on edges into x. Valid, f is a flow.
0037-0044 Same for g. Valid.
0045-0058 Subtracts (1) from (2) termwise to get (*): sum over out-edges of (g-f) equals sum over in-edges of (g-f). Valid (finite sums, linearity).
0059-0060 Page artifact, no content.
0061-0065 Key identity for an out-edge (x,y): g(x,y)-f(x,y)=h(x,y)-h(y,x), justified by the two construction cases (one of the two residual arcs of that edge is 0). Correct; the arcs referenced are the forward/backward arcs of the edge (x,y).
0066-0067 Mirror identity for an in-edge (y,x): g(y,x)-f(y,x)=h(y,x)-h(x,y), with h(y,x) the forward and h(x,y) the backward residual arc of edge (y,x). Correct by the same case analysis.
0068-0076 Substitutes these identities into (*): LHS becomes sum over out-edges of [h(x,y)-h(y,x)], RHS sum over in-edges of [h(y,x)-h(x,y)]. Correct substitution.
0077-0089 Splits both sides into four sums: A-B = C-D with A=sum_out h(x,y), B=sum_out h(y,x), C=sum_in h(y,x), D=sum_in h(x,y). Correct.
0090-0102 Rearranges to A+D = B+C. Verified algebraically: moving -B right and -D left gives exactly the displayed identity. Correct.
0103-0105 Identifies A+D as the total outflow of h at x in Gf (forward residual arcs of out-edges plus backward residual arcs of in-edges = all residual arcs leaving x) and B+C as the total inflow (backward residual arcs of out-edges plus forward residual arcs of in-edges = all residual arcs entering x). This enumeration is exact, each residual arc incident to x counted once. Correct.
0106-0113 Concludes conservation of h at x, and since x was an arbitrary non-terminal vertex, at all intermediate vertices. Valid generalization.
0114-0115 Defines |h| as net outflow of h at s (= net inflow at t by (ii)). Standard definition, consistent with (ii).
0116-0117 Asserts that since f,g are (s,t)-flows, s carries no inflow and t no outflow. This is a convention-dependent premise (assumed outright in e.g. Kleinberg-Tardos-style flow-network definitions); under it the next display is exact. It is the weakest point of the write-up, but it is a standard convention rather than a false inference, and the argument goes through verbatim without it after replacing each source sum by the net (out minus in) sum. Accepted.
0118-0125 |f| and |g| equal the sums of f resp. g over edges leaving s. Correct under the convention just invoked.
0126-0130 Subtracts: |g|-|f| = sum over edges (s,y) of [g(s,y)-f(s,y)]. Correct.
0131-0132 Page artifact, no content.
0133-0134 Each term g(s,y)-f(s,y) equals h(s,y)-h(y,s) by the identity established at 0063. Correct.
0135-0136 Case gloss; the phrase 'exactly one of h(s,y), h(y,s) is positive' is imprecise when g(s,y)=f(s,y) (both are then 0), but the operative claim -- that the difference equals g(s,y)-f(s,y) -- is correct in all three cases, so the imprecision is harmless.
0137-0150 Rewrites |g|-|f| as sum_y h(s,y) - sum_y h(y,s), extending the index set from edges leaving s to all y. Legitimate: vertices y with no residual arc to or from s contribute 0, and (under the convention of 0116) there are no edges into s, so no extra residual arcs at s are picked up.
0151-0158 Identifies that quantity with the net outflow of h at s, i.e. |h|=|g|-|f|. Correct given the definition at 0114-0115.
0159-0160 |h|>0 since |g|>|f|. Correct, and only a remark.
0161-0163 Combines (i) capacity, (ii) conservation, (iii) value to conclude Gf admits a feasible (s,t)-flow of value |g|-|f|. Exactly the required statement; all three ingredients were established.
Overall: the construction h = (g-f)^+ routed on forward residual arcs and (f-g)^+ on backward residual arcs is the canonical proof, every algebraic manipulation checks out, and the only blemishes (the source-has-no-inflow convention at 0116, the 'exactly one is positive' slip at 0136, and the overloaded h(u,v) notation when antiparallel edges exist) do not break any step's conclusion.
